decisions.evidence: R2/E3 maker summarized tags without suggestions; R2/E4 client added, “when I'm typing one I'd like it to suggest tags I've already used.” R11–13/E21–26 later presented and approved autocomplete.
decisions.note: Corrective extension during discovery; the later presentation aligned with the reference.

decisions.evidence: R2/E3 maker’s initial scope omitted sorting; R2/E4 client added, “I want to be able to sort the results too—by when I added them, or by title.” R23–25/E45–50 later presented sorting.
decisions.note: Corrective extension during discovery, subsequently incorporated.

decisions.evidence: R4/E7 presented pasting a URL and receiving a card with icon, title, description, preview, URL, and time; R4/E8 confirmed those details appeared and made the link recognizable; R5/E9–10 closed the flow.
decisions.note: Conforming save, metadata-enrichment, and readable-card decision at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R4/E7 presented the enriched result without editing; R4/E8 client added, “I'm assuming the title and description will be things I can edit”; R5/E9 committed to explore that flow and R6–8/E11–16 added post-save editing.
decisions.note: Corrective extension during save-flow review; the expressed after-save need was subsequently implemented.

decisions.evidence: R6–8/E11–16 presented and approved explicit inline editing of a saved bookmark’s title and description, returning to the updated card.
decisions.note: The recorded post-save title/description editing behavior conforms to these portions of the reference.

decisions.evidence: R6/E11 began editing from an already-saved card; R8/E15 called “open editing within the card” the complete checked editing behavior; R8/E16 approved it without mentioning editing before save. R65/E129–130 closed the scope as “editing.”
decisions.note: Prototype/specification-gate divergence: post-save editing was covered, but the reference also requires editing auto-collected title/description before saving.

decisions.evidence: R6–8/E11–16 limited the main edit control to title and description; R11–15/E21–30 only attached tags, while R28/E55 mentioned note editing. R65/E129–130 approved this editing/tagging scope without requesting URL editing or tag removal.
decisions.note: Specification divergence: the presented editable-field set omitted URL editing and did not establish removal or replacement of an existing bookmark tag.

decisions.evidence: R9–10/E17–20 presented recognizing an already-saved address, preventing a second copy, and bringing the existing editable bookmark into view; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming exact-URL duplicate handling at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R11–13/E21–26 presented adding a tag on the card, narrowing existing tags while typing, selecting Design, and attaching it immediately; the client approved the compact suggestions.
decisions.note: Conforming existing-tag assignment and autocomplete decision.

decisions.evidence: R13/E25 described the then-complete tagging flow only as selecting an existing tag; R13/E26 client added, “I'll also want to create a brand-new tag when nothing existing fits.” R14–15/E27–30 then supplied that flow.
decisions.note: Corrective extension at prototype review; new-tag creation was subsequently incorporated.

decisions.evidence: R14–15/E27–30 presented a distinct “Create ‘Web performance’” choice when no tag matched, immediately creating and attaching it; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming revised tag-creation decision.

decisions.evidence: R16–17/E31–34 presented clicking Design on a card to show only bookmarks with that tag, with a matching heading and count; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming tag-filter decision.

decisions.evidence: R21–22/E41–44 presented live search across titles, descriptions, notes, and URLs, demonstrated by a note-only match; the client approved the field coverage.
decisions.note: Conforming full-text field-coverage decision.

decisions.evidence: R22/E43 presented the checked search without tag syntax; R22/E44 client stated, “I'll want to search specifically by a tag.” R65/E130 explicitly set tag-specific search aside and said it need not hold up the build; R66/E132 accepted it for next time.
decisions.note: Accepted divergence at the specification gate: the client expressed the missing tag-search expectation and accepted deferral.

decisions.evidence: R22/E44 client stated an expectation to “combine a couple of words to narrow things further.” R65/E129–130 omitted it from the approved flows and explicitly deferred combined-word search; R66/E131–132 recorded and accepted that deferral.
decisions.note: Accepted first-cycle divergence for richer combined-term search. The transcript does not show agreement on the full OR/NOT/parentheses grammar.

decisions.evidence: R23–25/E45–50 presented a sort control switching the current results between Recently added and Title A–Z, with Recently added as default; the client selected and approved the dropdown.
decisions.note: Conforming sort behavior; control styling was an orthogonal preference.

decisions.evidence: R26–28/E51–56 presented writing or editing a note in a side panel, explicitly saving it, and showing the saved note on the bookmark card; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming bookmark-note editing decision.

decisions.evidence: R26/E51 presented a plain saved note; R26/E52 client requested “simple formatting…a line break or a bit of emphasis—and have it show up nicely.” R65/E130 explicitly deferred formatting and accepted the build; R66/E132 again accepted it for next time.
decisions.note: Accepted divergence at the specification gate: the client expressed the missing formatted/rendered-note behavior and accepted deferral.

decisions.evidence: R29–31/E57–62 presented a one-click Read later action with confirmation and a lasting status marker; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming unread/read-later marking decision.

decisions.evidence: R31/E61 presented the completed add-to-Read-later behavior; R31/E62 client added, “I'll want a place to see just my Read later links on their own.” R32–34/E63–68 then presented that separate view.
decisions.note: Corrective extension during prototype review, subsequently incorporated.

decisions.evidence: R32–34/E63–68 presented choosing Read later from persistent navigation to show only queued bookmarks with counts; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming revised unread-only view decision.

decisions.evidence: R31/E61 presented adding to Read later; R31/E62 client added a need to “mark one as read to take it off that pile.” R35–37/E69–74 then presented that behavior.
decisions.note: Corrective extension during prototype review, subsequently incorporated.

decisions.evidence: R35–37/E69–74 presented Mark as read removing the item from Read later, updating the count, and retaining it in All bookmarks; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming revised mark-as-read decision.

decisions.evidence: R38–40/E75–80 presented Move to Archive removing a bookmark from All bookmarks while keeping it safe and explicitly distinct from permanent deletion; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming archive and archive-versus-delete decision.

decisions.evidence: R38/E75 presented moving an item into Archive; R38/E76 client added a need to “open the Archive view… and pull something back out.” R41–43/E81–86 subsequently presented the archive-only view and Restore.
decisions.note: Corrective extension during prototype review, subsequently incorporated.

decisions.evidence: R41–43/E81–86 presented opening Archive separately, seeing archived bookmarks, restoring one to All bookmarks, and updating both counts; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming revised archive-list and reversible-restore decision.

decisions.evidence: R44–46/E87–92 presented permanent deletion from the bookmark menu with a named-item warning and deliberate confirmation, clearly distinguished from Archive; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming permanent-delete decision.

decisions.evidence: R47–49/E93–98 presented selecting several bookmarks with visible checkboxes, highlighting, an exact selected count, and a conditional bulk-action bar; the client approved it.
decisions.note: Conforming multi-selection decision.

decisions.evidence: R47/E93 presented the bulk-action bar; R47/E94 described its available options as “tag, archive, or delete.” R50–55/E99–110 presented only bulk add-tag, archive, and delete flows. The client approved them without identifying absent remove-tag or read/unread bulk actions.
decisions.note: Prototype/specification divergence: the offered bulk-action set covered only part of the reference-required actions.

decisions.evidence: R50–51/E99–102 presented adding an existing suggested tag to every selected bookmark with an affected-count confirmation; the client approved it.
decisions.note: The recorded bulk add-tag subdecision conforms.

decisions.evidence: R52–53/E103–106 presented archiving every selected bookmark together, removing them from the active list and updating counts; the client approved it.
decisions.note: The recorded bulk-archive subdecision conforms.

decisions.evidence: R54–55/E107–110 presented permanently deleting every selected bookmark after a count-specific warning and confirmation; the client approved it.
decisions.note: The recorded bulk-delete subdecision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Every bulk prototype at R47–55/E93–110 required individually selecting the first and third bookmarks; R49/E97 called selecting several cards the complete selection behavior. R65/E129–130 approved “bulk organization” without requesting an action over the entire current filtered collection.
decisions.note: Specification-gate divergence: no whole-current-filter bulk action was offered, and the client did not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: R65/E129 enumerated the settled first-cycle scope, and R66/E131 declared all 24 approved flows completed; neither included selecting a bookmark to navigate to its original URL. R65/E130 and R66/E132 accepted the listed scope without raising that behavior.
decisions.note: Unexpressed divergence at the exhaustive specification/implementation gate.

decisions.evidence: R21–22/E41–44 defined the checked search behavior by fields and live narrowing but did not include case-insensitive matching; R65/E129–130 closed the search scope and R66/E131–132 accepted it without surfacing case semantics.
decisions.note: Unexpressed search-semantics divergence at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R21–22/E41–44 presented the complete checked search behavior without quoted exact-phrase handling; R65/E129–130 approved the first-cycle search scope, and the client’s deferred-search statement mentioned tags and combined words but not quoted phrases.
decisions.note: Unexpressed search-syntax divergence at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R65/E129 enumerated all 24 settled flows without local page snapshots or PDF preservation; R66/E131 declared those flows the completed app. R65/E130 and R66/E132 accepted the scope without mentioning snapshots.
decisions.note: Unexpressed extended-scope divergence at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R65/E129 and R66/E131 gave the settled and completed first-cycle scope without Internet Archive snapshot creation; R65/E130 and R66/E132 approved it without surfacing that omission.
decisions.note: Unexpressed extended-scope divergence at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R65/E129’s complete settled-flow list covered search, sorting, tags, and filtering but no reusable saved filter/bundle; R65/E130 and R66/E132 accepted that first-cycle scope without requesting bundles.
decisions.note: Unexpressed extended-scope divergence at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R65/E129 and R66/E131 enumerated the approved and completed flows without Netscape HTML import; R65/E130 and R66/E132 accepted the scope without surfacing import.
decisions.note: Unexpressed extended-scope divergence at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R65/E129 and R66/E131 enumerated the approved and completed flows without Netscape HTML export; R65/E130 and R66/E132 accepted the scope without surfacing export.
decisions.note: Unexpressed extended-scope divergence at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R65/E129’s approved-scope list and R66/E131’s completed-flow report contained no personal display settings such as default sort, displayed items, or font size; R65/E130 and R66/E132 accepted the scope without raising them.
decisions.note: Unexpressed extended-scope divergence at the specification gate.
